Ski Instructor here:

Skis are designed to pop off when a certain amount of torque is applied to the binding and pop off before you hurt yourself. There's a formula you use to calculate how tight they should be. This is so that you don't fall out of them too early, or have them fused to your feet. It all depends on how good you are, how heavy you are and so on... For a normal person, this is pretty simple. The problem is, that they're so heavy that you can't use a release setting that would be normal for a beginner, they'd just fall out of the skis instantly. So instead the skis have to be cranked up to the levels that an Olympic racer would use, (basically bolting the thing down) so of course they can't get them off.
